title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Issuing the "Revised Supplementary Opinions on the Issue of Misappropriation of Public Funds for Personal Use or for Illegal Activities to Be Treated as Embezzlement"
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Supreme People's Procuratorate

Notice on Issuing the "Revised Supplementary Opinions on the Issue of Treating Misappropriation of Public Funds for Personal Use or for Illegal Activities as Embezzlement"

Fa (Yan) Fa [1987] No. 6

To the Higher People's Courts and People's Procuratorates of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court and Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army; the Railway Transport Higher Court and Railway Transport Procuratorate:

The Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate hereby issue to you the Revised Supplementary Opinions on the issue of "Treating Misappropriation of Public Funds for Personal Use or for Illegal Activities as Embezzlement" in the "Answers to Several Questions on the Specific Application of Laws in the Current Handling of Economic Crimes (for Trial Implementation)" jointly issued on July 18, 1985, for your reference and implementation in your work.

Attachment: Revised Supplementary Opinions on the Issue of "Treating Misappropriation of Public Funds for Personal Use or for Illegal Activities as Embezzlement"

March 14, 1987

Revised Supplementary Opinions on the Issue of "Treating Misappropriation of Public Funds for Personal Use or for Illegal Activities as Embezzlement"

The Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate jointly issued the "Answers to Several Questions on the Specific Application of Laws in the Current Handling of Economic Crimes (for Trial Implementation)" on July 18, 1985. After more than one year of trial implementation, the issue of "Treating Misappropriation of Public Funds for Personal Use or for Illegal Activities as Embezzlement" therein is now revised and supplemented as follows:

I. Issues concerning the determination of and differentiated treatment for treating misappropriation of public funds for personal use as embezzlement.

Misappropriation of public funds generally constitutes a violation of financial and economic discipline and shall be handled by the competent authority in accordance with administrative discipline; where the harm is serious, it constitutes a crime.

State personnel, personnel of collective economic organizations, and persons entrusted by state organs, enterprises, institutions, and people's organizations to engage in public service, who, by taking advantage of their position, without authorization misappropriate public funds for personal use (including use by themselves or lending to others), where the amount is relatively large and the funds are not repaid after more than six months; or where the amount is huge; or where the funds are used for illegal activities and the amount is relatively large; the nature of such conduct constitutes illegal possession of public property and shall be punished as the crime of embezzlement.

In determining a case of misappropriation of public funds for personal use as embezzlement, a specific analysis and differentiated treatment shall be made for each specific case based on factors such as the amount misappropriated, the duration of the misappropriation, whether repayment has been made, the amount repaid, the purpose of use, whether the misappropriator gained profit, and the extent of loss and harm caused to the state and the collective.

(1) Misappropriation of public funds for personal use, where the amount is relatively large and the funds are not repaid after more than six months, shall be punished as the crime of embezzlement.

Where the misappropriation period has exceeded six months, but repayment is made before the case is discovered (i.e., before discovery by the judicial organs, the competent authority, or relevant units), generally it shall not be punished as the crime of embezzlement.

(2) Misappropriation of public funds for personal use, where the amount is huge, shall be punished as the crime of embezzlement regardless of whether the misappropriation period exceeds six months.

Where repayment is made before the case is discovered and the loss caused to the state and the collective is minimal, generally it shall not be punished as the crime of embezzlement.

(3) Misappropriation of public funds for individuals to engage in illegal activities such as speculation, smuggling, gambling, etc., where the amount is relatively large, shall be punished as the crime of embezzlement regardless of whether the misappropriation period exceeds six months. Where the illegal activities constitute other crimes, the offender shall be punished for multiple crimes in accordance with the law.

Where repayment is made before the case is discovered, a lighter or mitigated punishment may be imposed; where the misappropriation period is short and the harm is minimal, punishment may also be exempted. Where the misappropriator did not know that the user was using the misappropriated funds to carry out illegal activities, punishment shall be imposed in accordance with item (1) above.

(4) State personnel who, by taking advantage of their authority over credit in their positions, fraudulently obtain loans in the name of others (or units), obtain loans under false names, use their authority to coerce others (or units) into granting loans, or intercept part of the loan for personal use when handling loans, also constitute misappropriation of public funds for personal use. Where such conduct meets the standards for criminal liability set forth in items (1), (2), and (3) above, it shall be punished as the crime of embezzlement, and differentiated treatment shall be applied according to the different circumstances in the three items above.

(5) Misappropriation of public property (goods) for individuals to engage in profit-making activities or illegal activities, where the conduct meets the standards set forth in items (2) and (3) above, shall be punished as the crime of embezzlement.

(6) In a case where misappropriation of public funds for use by others is treated as embezzlement, if the user conspires with the misappropriator, instigates or participates in planning the illegal acquisition of the misappropriated funds, the user shall be punished as an accomplice.

(7) Any bribes received from misappropriating public funds for the use of others shall be recovered. Where such conduct constitutes the crime of accepting bribes or the crime of offering bribes, the offender shall be punished for the crime of accepting bribes or the crime of offering bribes respectively.

(8) Any profits and illegal gains obtained from misappropriating public funds for individuals (including accomplices) to engage in profit-making activities or illegal activities shall be recovered.

II. Issues concerning the amount standards and sentencing for treating misappropriation of public funds for personal use as the crime of embezzlement.

Cases where misappropriation of public funds for personal use is treated as the crime of embezzlement differ from the crime of embezzlement constituted by directly illegally taking possession of public property through means such as falsifying accounts or destroying documents in terms of circumstances and degree of social harm. Therefore, the amount standards and sentencing should also differ.

(1) In cases where misappropriation of public funds for personal use is treated as the crime of embezzlement, the standard for calculating the misappropriation amount shall generally be higher than the amount standard for the crime of embezzlement. The starting point for "relatively large amount" shall be misappropriation of 5,000 yuan to 10,000 yuan; the starting point for "huge amount" shall be misappropriation of 50,000 yuan; and the starting point for "particularly huge amount" shall be misappropriation of 100,000 yuan to 200,000 yuan. The Higher People's Courts and People's Procuratorates of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, based on the actual conditions of their respective regions and with reference to the above amounts, stipulate the specific amount standards to be applied within their regions.

(2) In terms of sentencing, Article 155 of the Criminal Law shall apply. Where the amount misappropriated is relatively large, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention; where the amount is huge and the circumstances are serious, or where the amount is particularly huge, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years; where the amount is particularly huge and the circumstances are particularly serious, the offender shall be sentenced to life imprisonment; in individual cases where the harm to the state and the people is particularly serious, the death penalty may be imposed. The amount standard for treating misappropriation as embezzlement shall be considered in conjunction with other circumstances comprehensively. Where the offender actively repays the misappropriated funds after the case is discovered and the loss caused to the state and the collective is minimal, a lighter, mitigated, or exempted punishment shall also be imposed in accordance with the law.

(3) Where public funds are misappropriated for personal use on multiple occasions, and misappropriated funds from a later occasion are used to repay misappropriated funds from an earlier occasion, with each occasion of misappropriation not exceeding six months, the misappropriation period shall be calculated from the first occasion and accumulated continuously until the cessation of the misappropriation conduct. The amount for calculating the misappropriation to be treated as embezzlement shall be determined based on the actual amount outstanding at the end.

III. Issues concerning the time limits for handling cases where misappropriation of public funds for personal use is treated as the crime of embezzlement.

In cases where the misappropriated public funds had been repaid prior to July 18, 1985, the date of issuance of the "Answers to Several Questions on the Specific Application of Laws in the Current Handling of Economic Crimes (for Trial Implementation)" by the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate, or cases that had already been dealt with by the competent authority or judicial organs, shall not be pursued further.

For cases adjudicated after the issuance of the above "Answers (for Trial Implementation)" but before the issuance of this document, in accordance with the spirit of the above "Answers (for Trial Implementation)," generally no changes shall be made. Where the basic facts and basic nature were indeed incorrectly determined, corrections shall be made. For cases that have not yet been handled or are being handled after the issuance of this document, they shall be handled in accordance with the spirit of this document.

March 14, 1987
